text_blocks.snippet: A complete blood count (CBC) can be a helpful tool in detecting and monitoring certain types of cancer, particularly blood cancers like leukemia and lymphoma, and in assessing how cancer and its treatments affect a patient's overall health. While a CBC is not typically used to diagnose solid tumor cancers like breast or lung cancer, it can provide valuable information about a patient's health status and response to treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: A complete blood count (CBC) can be a helpful tool in detecting and monitoring certain types of cancer, particularly blood cancers like leukemia and lymphoma

text_blocks.snippet: How CBCs are used in cancer:

list.title: Detecting Blood Cancers:
list.snippet: A CBC can reveal abnormal levels or types of blood cells that may indicate leukemia or lymphoma.

list.title: Assessing Spread to Bone Marrow:
list.snippet: CBC results can help determine if cancer has spread to the bone marrow, which is where blood cells are produced.

list.title: Monitoring Treatment Effects:
list.snippet: CBCs are frequently used to track how cancer treatments, such as chemotherapy, are impacting a patient's blood cell counts and overall health.

list.title: Identifying Other Conditions:
list.snippet: CBCs can also detect other conditions, like anemia (low red blood cell count) or infections, which may occur alongside or as a result of cancer or its treatment.

list.title: Tracking Overall Health:
list.snippet: CBCs provide a snapshot of a patient's general health, which can be useful in managing cancer and its side effects.
Low red blood cell counts (anemia): Can be a sign of cancers that affect the bone marrow, or a side effect of cancer treatment.
Low white blood cell counts (neutropenia): Can indicate bone marrow involvement or be a side effect of chemotherapy.
High or low platelet counts: Can signal problems with blood clotting and bleeding, which may be associated with certain cancers or treatments.

list.title: Not a definitive diagnosis:
list.snippet: While a CBC can be suggestive, it's not a standalone diagnostic tool for most cancers.

list.title: Follow-up testing:
list.snippet: If a CBC raises concerns, further testing, such as tumor marker tests or imaging scans, will likely be needed to confirm a diagnosis.

list.title: Monitoring during treatment:
list.snippet: CBCs are essential for monitoring patients during cancer treatment to identify and manage potential complications related to low blood counts.

list.title: Individualized approach:
list.snippet: The interpretation of CBC results should always be done by a healthcare professional in the context of a patient's overall medical history and other test results.
